With cracked plaster and peeling paint, I considered what I could say. Water damage would've been the easy answer, but I opted for the truth: "My phone rang." As expected, these words settled somewhere beyond her reach, so she gave my comment its only sensible response: "Maybe you should turn down the ringer." "Come here, let me explain why I hate phones, and why my father is to blame. He was a troubled man," I said, because that's how it had been said to me. She listened with attentive eyes, but I knew she'd be confused by what I said next: "And he'd play Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera. Over and over." She lowered her head in search of a link and looked up when she found one. "Is that solitaire?" This time I allowed a smile. "Sometimes he'd conduct an invisible orchestra, waving arms in an erratic fashion, and sometimes he'd sit and listen. But Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera, that one commanded a different reaction. From the start, he stood at full attention, motionless until the end. It went like this for a long time, then he left."

"I soon became his replacement. I'd sit in the study and listen to his music. One evening mother said he wanted to talk to me. I asked if I was going to see him and she said that he'd call. I asked if I could use the phone in his study and she said I could." At this point my companion, attentive as ever, offered her second assumption of the evening, and though more likely than the first, it was just as wrong: "And he never called and that's why you hate phones." No, that's not why. "When mother told me he was on the line, I rushed to the study and dropped the needle on Nulla in Mundo Pax Sincera, then picked up the phone. He didn't say hello or ask how I was, he only said that there's no peace in the world. He'd looked, it wasn't there, not for him." With her final assumption, she came closer to the truth: "So phones remind you of your father, and that's why you hate them."

"That's part of it," I said, "but there's more. He said he could hear Vivaldi in the background and told me to keep listening, that aria was on to something. Then he said goodbye to me and mother and everyone else. Forever. He found his peace." The music prevented a silence that would've felt more comfortable, then it finally stopped and I let the silence prevail. And there we sat, speaking without speaking, until the silence was shattered by a ring. I stood and walked to the phone, picked it up, not just the receiver, but all of it, and paused to admire the artistry.

What is the tone of the passage?

The passage talks about the gloomy past of the speaker.

Optimistic: When writing in an optimistic tone, you're conveying a sense of hope and a positive outlook for the future.

Dispirited: low in spirit or enthusiasm; downhearted or depressed; discouraged.

Romantic: This kind of tone is, as you might anticipate, fantastical and exaggerated. These sentences could seem entertaining to read, yet the content is implausible.

After reading the passage it can be said that the tone of the passage is 'Dispirited'.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Ruchi said that she was going to cast her vote.
options_en: Ruchi said to, "I was going to cast my vote".
Ruchi said, "I am going to cast my vote".
Ruchi said, "She was going to cast my vote".
Ruchi said, "I was going to cast her vote".
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'She was' becomes 'I am', 'her' becomes 'my' and 'that' is removed.

Accordingly, the option that has the correct Direct speech sentence is (b), Ruchi said, "I am going to cast my vote".

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The Rosetta Stone is a large granodiorite stele that has become one of the most famous archaeological artifacts in the entire world since its discovery.

B. Its decipherment was the essential key to our modern understanding of ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, unlocking the secrets of a long-lost civilization for scholars.

C. The inscription on the stone presents a single decree issued at Memphis, Egypt, in 196 BC, but it is uniquely inscribed in three different scripts.

D. It was accidentally discovered in 1799 by a French soldier named Pierre-François Bouchard during Napoleon's campaign in Egypt and Syria.
questions.solution_en:
Sentence A is the most suitable opening as it introduces the "Rosetta Stone" and its general significance. Sentence D logically follows by providing the historical context of its discovery, mentioning when and by whom "It" (the stone) was found. Sentence C then elaborates on the stone's content, describing the "inscription on the stone" and its unique feature of having three scripts. Finally, sentence B provides the concluding statement by explaining the profound impact of the stone's decipherment ("Its decipherment..."), which logically comes after the description of its contents. The sequence ADCB presents a clear flow from introduction to discovery, description, and finally, significance.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Scientists have recently discovered a new species of marine life in the unexplored depths of the ocean.

questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb ['been' here] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Perfect. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Perfect.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arya has bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

A new horse has been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.q_en:
Directions :Read the following comprehension and answer the questions that follow.

Subhas Chandra Bose, a prominent Indian nationalist leader, was convinced that India could not achieve independence without the use of force, and he believed that a military campaign was necessary to achieve this goal. In 1942, Bose formed the Indian National Army (INA) with the help of the Japanese. Bose travelled to Japan in 1941 to seek their support in the struggle against British rule in India. The Japanese were interested in having Bose's help in their own efforts to expand their influence in Southeast Asia. Bose's vision was to create a military force to fight against the British in India with the help of Japanese weapons and training. The INA was formed in Singapore in September 1942 with the slogan 'Jai Hind' (Victory to India). The INA consisted of soldiers who were primarily from the Indian community in Southeast Asia. They were trained by Japanese officers and were equipped with Japanese weapons. The INA fought alongside Japanese forces in Burma and other parts of Southeast Asia during World War II. Bose's leadership of the INA and his military campaigns against the British in India made him a popular figure among many Indians. The consequences of the formation of the INA were significant. The INA's campaigns against the British in India and the Indian soldiers' role in the Burma campaign had a psychological impact on the British forces. The British were shocked that Indian soldiers had turned against them, undermining their confidence in maintaining control over India. The INA also had a significant impact on the Indian independence movement. Boses vision of a socialist India with equal rights for all citizens inspired many Indians. The INA became a symbol of the struggle against British colonialism, and Bose's slogan of 'Jai Hind' became a rallying cry for the independence movement. However, the INA's military campaigns were not successful in achieving their goal of freeing India from British rule. The INA suffered significant losses in battles, and their efforts were undermined by the Japanese surrender in 1945.

What ultimately undermined the INA's efforts to free India from British rule?
options_en: The lack of support from the Indian and British people
The inferior military tactics of the British forces

According to the passage: "However, the INA's military campaigns were not successful in achieving their goal of freeing India from British rule. The INA suffered significant losses in battles, and their efforts were undermined by the Japanese surrender in 1945."

This clearly identifies the Japanese surrender as a critical factor that undermined the INA's efforts, since the INA was heavily dependent on Japanese support for weapons, training, and coordination.

I am sure that / the postman would be / coming shortly / to deliver the letter.
questions.solution_en:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'the postman would be'. The error lies in the usage of the word "would". "Will" implies certainty, while "would" implies a possibility. Since the sentence is expressing future certainty ("I am sure that..."), it should use the future tense "will be" instead of the conditional "would be". Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: I am sure that the postman will be coming shortly to deliver the letter.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Transport Corporation has decided to discontinue ______ bus service for private schools.
questions.solution_en:
'Bus service' is a singular noun phrase, so we can eliminate the plural demonstrative adjectives 'these' and 'those'. We need a possessive determiner to qualify the noun 'bus service'. "It's" is the contracted form of "it is/it has" which is not required here. So, option (a) is eliminated as it is grammatically incorrect. The possessive determiner 'its' is the one that fits correctly in the blank. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

Demonstrative Adjectives: Demonstrative adjectives include "this", "that", "these" and "those". These modify or describe a noun and come before a noun while 'demonstrative pronouns' replace a noun. Example: "I like that T-shirt of yours".
questions.solution_hi:
'Bus service' is a singular noun phrase, so we can eliminate the plural demonstrative adjectives 'these' and 'those'. We need a possessive determiner to qualify the noun 'bus service'. "It's" is the contracted form of "it is/it has" which is not required here. So, option (a) is eliminated as it is grammatically incorrect. The possessive determiner 'its' is the one that fits correctly in the blank. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

Demonstrative Adjectives: Demonstrative adjectives include "this", "that", "these" and "those". These modify or describe a noun and come before a noun while 'demonstrative pronouns' replace a noun. Example: "I like that T-shirt of yours".

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. Note: This is about the impact of smartphone use on teenage brain development.

A. Excessive smartphone use can disrupt healthy brain development by weakening connections between brain cells, making it harder to regulate emotional reactions and other brain functions.

B. Smartphone use can also make it harder for teenagers to focus and avoid distractions, thereby increasing their dependence on digital devices.

C. Understanding the impact of smartphone use on teenage brain development is crucial.
questions.solution_en:
Sentence 'C' serves as an introduction, setting up the importance of the topic. Sentence 'A' explains the negative effects of smartphone use on brain development, expanding on the idea introduced in the first sentence. Sentence 'B' follows and provides additional details on how smartphone use affects focus and leads to dependence on digital devices, continuing from the explanation in sentence A.

So, the correct order is CAB.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice:

Historians tell us how this country was divided into three.
options_en: We are told by historians how this country has been divided into three.
We are told by historians how this country divided into three.
We are told by historians how this country was divided into three.
We have been told by historians how this country was divided into three.
questions.solution_en:
In passive voice, the subject receiving the action (we) comes first.

"Are told" keeps the verb in the present tense to match the original sentence.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

John said, "I have received the package."
options_en: John said that he has received the package.
John said that he had received the package.
John said that he received the package.
John said that he receives the package.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

"Said" will change to "said that".

"I have" will be changed to "he had".

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): John said that he had received the package.

questions.q_en:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given.

She likes to made people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
options_en: She likes to makes people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
She likes to making people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
She likes to be make people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
She likes to make people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.
questions.solution_en:
The infinitive marker 'To' is always followed by a base form of the verb, so the use of 'made/makes/making' [V2/V3, V5, V4 respectively] will be incorrect here. 'To + be' is followed by a participle form of the verb which is not the case in option (c) ['make' is the base verb], therefore, it will be incorrect as well. The grammatically correct sentence is mentioned in option (d).

The correct sentence is - 'She likes to make people lose their cool by starting belligerent political arguments.'

Hence, option (d) is correct.

NOTE/-

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below: Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground. Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion. The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect. The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes completed action or state of the thing spoken of. A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n. One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The customer orders are carefully processed by the staff every morning to ensure timely delivery. The entire inventory is thoroughly checked by the manager on a daily basis to avoid any discrepancies.
options_en: The staff carefully processed the customer orders every morning to ensure timely delivery. The manager thoroughly checked the entire inventory on a daily basis to avoid any discrepancies.
The staff carefully has processed the customer orders every morning to ensure timely delivery. The manager has thoroughly checked the entire inventory on a daily basis to avoid any discrepancies.
The staff carefully processes the customer orders every morning to ensure timely delivery. The manager thoroughly checks the entire inventory on a daily basis to avoid any discrepancies.
The staff is carefully processing the customer orders every morning to ensure timely delivery. The manager is thoroughly checking the entire inventory on a daily basis to avoid any discrepancies.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['are' and 'is' respectively] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Indefinite tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V1/V5 + Object.

For example:

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

She likes you. (Active Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option c): The staff carefully processes the customer orders every morning to ensure timely delivery. The manager thoroughly checks the entire inventory on a daily basis to avoid any discrepancies.
